newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Umax-M'bishi unit to invest T$12b in Taiwan chips.
newsitem.headline: Umax-M'bishi unit to invest T$12b in Taiwan chips.

text.p: Taiwan's Powerchip Co, a joint venture of Umax-Elite group and Mitsubishi Electric, said on Friday it would invest T$12 billion to upgrade one Taiwan microchip plant and build another.

Powerchip said the expansions, to be completed by the end of 1998, would enable the firm to upgrade production to advanced 64-megabit dynamic random access memory chips from the current 16-megabit DRAMs.

"We will be upgrading our first plant and building the second plant simultaneously and they both will receive technological assistance from Mitsubishi," Powerchip spokeswoman Kiki Chen said by telephone.
Under the expansion plans, Powerchip envisages boosting the production capacity of its first plant to 25,000 DRAMs a month from 15,000.
The second plant, scheduled to begin construction in the fourth quarter, would produce 10,000 64-megabit DRAMs a month, Chen said.
"The first plant will continue to make both 16- and 64-megabit DRAMs, while the second one will be making the advanced chips exclusively," she said.
Powerchip, in a statement, called the plan a "giant leap for domestic chip technology and "a symbol of the start to the 64-megabit battle."

Powerchip is one of several Taiwan chipmakers enlisting technological assistance from Japanese allies to compete against Korean giants like Samsung Electronics in the global market for advanced DRAMs.
